entries.topic: Kook lineage, Religious Zionism as party and movement, Kahanism, and religious opposition to maximalism

claims.text: Abraham Isaac Kook (7 Sep 1865 – 1 Sep 1935): rabbi in Jaffa from 1904/05; first Ashkenazi Chief Rabbi of Mandatory Palestine 1921; founded Mercaz HaRav in Jerusalem 1924; respected secular Zionists and hailed them as 'hastening the messianic deliverance'; supported settlement of the land.

Zvi Yehuda Kook (23 Apr 1891 – 9 Mar 1982), son of A.I. Kook; administrative director of Mercaz HaRav from 1923, rosh yeshiva from 1952; hailed the 1967 victory; after 1973 'vigorously opposed proposals to yield territory'; said 'No one, no prime minister, has the authority to renounce any part of the country'; opposed Begin's Sinai negotiations; Gush Emunim founded by his students.

Zvi Yehuda Kook's speech at Mercaz HaRav on Israel's 19th Independence Day (1967), weeks before the Six-Day War: 'Where is our Hebron? Are we forgetting it?'; repeated 'My land was divided'; students later gave it prophetic status and distributed tens of thousands of copies; he died about six weeks before the Sinai withdrawal was completed in 1982.

Smotrich (NPR, 21 Mar 2025): 'My long-term desire is for the state of Israel to be governed according to the Torah'; Persico places him on the far right of religious Zionism; consults rabbis; objects to the word annexation ('implies taking something that isn't yours'); 11% voted for his list in 2022.

Smotrich quoted in ARTE documentary 'Israel: Extremists in Power' (reported 10 Oct 2024): 'It is written that the future of Jerusalem is to expand to Damascus'; the wider list of countries is the outlet's paraphrase; no clarification reported.

Reuters 7 Aug 2026: Religious Zionism holds seven of 120 seats; ran with Ben-Gvir's party in 2022 (joint 14 seats); polls indicate it would struggle to pass 3.5% threshold for the 27 Oct 2026 election; Smotrich supported a July 2026 bill to prevent arrests of Haredi draft evaders (passed, blocked by Supreme Court); former supporters said he 'no longer represents the values of Religious Zionism'.

JPost 13 Aug 2026: Smotrich rejected a joint run with Ben-Gvir; RZP polling about five seats, just over the threshold. ToI 15 Jun 2026: Ben-Gvir said the parties must run separately; Zman Yisrael poll gave Otzma Yehudit eight seats and RZP below threshold.

Kach founded by Meir Kahane 1971; one seat 1984; disqualified 1988 (aims 'manifestly racist'); banned by Israeli cabinet 1994 after Goldstein's massacre of 29 Palestinians at the Cave of the Patriarchs; platform: 'Immediate annexation of every part of Israel that is in our hands'; US removed from terror list May 2022.

Oz VeShalom (c. 1975) and Netivot Shalom: religious Zionist peace groups that backed the 1990s peace process incl. a Palestinian state; Meimad founded 1988 by Rabbi Yehuda Amital (head of Yeshivat Har Etzion), open to territorial compromise, held that placing the Land above all values contradicts the Torah; 9 May 2003 manifesto by 170 religious Zionists urged giving up control of the territories.
Meimad founded 1 June 1988 by Amital; party from 1999; joined One Israel 1999 (seat taken by Michael Melchior); one seat 1999, 2003, 2006; centre-left on the conflict.

Rabbi Ovadia Yosef (Shas) ruled in 1979 that returning land for lasting peace is permitted under pikuach nefesh: 'nothing is more important than the saving of life'; Shas abstained on Oslo in 1993; he opposed the 2005 Gaza withdrawal.

Jewish Press (9 Oct 2013) published an undated letter, provenance unstated, said to show Yosef declared in c. 2003 that 'giving up land for peace has no validity in light of the current situation'; single-sourced.

Satmar's Joel Teitelbaum called Zionism 'a severe heresy and a rebellion against God'; Vayoel Moshe (1959) built on the Three Oaths; after 1967 his pamphlet held the war was no miracle and 'forbade prayer at the Wall or at the other occupied holy sites'; Satmar the largest Hasidic group (~26,000 households c. 2016).

entries.topic: Temple Mount status quo, Jordan's custodial role, Third Temple movements, changes 2023-2026

claims.text: After June 1967 Israel took control of the site while administration stayed with the Jordan-based Jerusalem Islamic Waqf; Israel barred its flag over the site; the Chief Rabbinate announced entering the Mount was forbidden to Jews (ritual impurity); Haredi authorities prohibit entry, some permit it, Religious Zionists consider visits a mitzvah.

Dec 2013: Chief Rabbis Lau and Yosef, with Amar and Rabinovitch, re-endorsed the ban, originally ruled by A.I. Kook; 'It has absolutely nothing to do with the political situation'; mostly national-religious groups encourage visits; 'hundreds of Jews visit the Temple Mount every month'.

Israel-Jordan treaty Art. 9: Israel respects 'the present special role of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in Muslim Holy shrines in Jerusalem'; 2013 Abbas-Abdullah agreement granted King Abdullah custodianship of Jerusalem holy sites; 24-25 Oct 2015 Kerry announced Israel accepted King Abdullah's 24-hour monitoring suggestion; Netanyahu reaffirmed 'upholding unchanged the status quo of the Temple Mount, in word and in practise'.

Temple Institute founded 1987 in Jerusalem by Rabbi Yisrael Ariel to establish the Third Temple; has made many of 90+ ritual items; Israeli Education and Culture ministries reportedly transferred NIS 300,000-700,000 over a decade (JPost via Wikipedia); 5 red heifers brought from the US Sept 2022; Maimonides reading 'controversial and has aroused substantial opposition'.

Red heifers flown from Texas 2022, donated by an evangelical farmer; Temple Institute and evangelical group Boneh Israel involved; raised at Shiloh; Jerusalem Affairs Ministry DG Netanel Isaac spoke at their arrival and the ministry funded development of the Mount of Olives ceremony area; Qassam spokesman Abu Obeida cited the heifers in his 100-days speech (Jan 2024).

Shin Bet summary (4 Mar 2025) listed among three factors in Hamas's timing Israel's handling of far-right Jewish religious activity at the Al-Aqsa compound, harsher prisoner treatment, and perceived social division.

26 Aug 2024: Ben-Gvir: 'The policies on the Temple Mount allow prayer, period'; PMO: 'there is no change to the status quo' and 'it is the government and the prime minister who determine policy on the Temple Mount'; Gallant called ascents 'dangerous, unnecessary and irresponsible'; status quo never legislated.

3 Aug 2025 (Tisha B'Av): Ben-Gvir openly led prayers on the Mount, first minister to do so; PMO: policy 'has not changed and will not change'; Jordan: 'an unacceptable provocation' and Israel has 'no sovereignty over the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque'; Saudi Arabia condemned; police enforcement had grown more lenient over three years.

4 Jan 2026: Netanyahu said allowing Jewish prayer 'does not breach' the status quo and that policy is coordinated with him; police have allowed Jewish prayers in the compound's eastern sector for two years; Deputy AG Gil Limon warned Ben-Gvir was unilaterally altering the status quo.

23 Jul 2026 (Tisha B'Av): Ben-Gvir: 'Jews praying, feeling like they're the owners of the place ... This has never happened before'; Jordan's foreign ministry: 'a desecration of the sanctity of the mosque, an escalation, a barbaric act, and unacceptable provocation'; Netanyahu's office did not immediately comment.

entries.topic: US Christian Zionist land theology: CUFI/Hagee, Huckabee 2026, polling, evangelical dissent

claims.text: Christians United for Israel: originally set up 1975 by David A. Lewis; incorporated by John Hagee 7 Feb 2006; HQ San Antonio; membership claims 1m (2012), 2m (2015), 5.1m (2018), 'over 10 million' (undated, self-reported); Netanyahu addressed summits (2010 by video; 2019 with Pence); criticised by the Middle East Council of Churches and J Street; Hagee apologised for claiming Hitler fulfilled God's plan.

Hagee, CUFI webcast 6 Jan 2011: 'Jerusalem should never be divided for any reason. It is the property of the people of Israel'; 'God did not make a covenant with Washington, D.C. He made a covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob'; cited Gen 13:14-17, 15:18-21, 17:7-8; correction: skeptical of land-for-peace but Israel's government should make its own decisions. Dissent: Richard Mouw (Fuller), Joel Hunter (Hagee's view reflects 'a limited portion of Christians who are millennial dispensationalists'); July 2007 NYT letter by 34 evangelical leaders backing a two-state solution.

Hagee: 'We do not seek to tell Israelis what to do'; 'Israelis - and they alone - have the right to make existential decisions about land and peace'; CUFI's action limited to 'asking the White House not to pressure Israel into making territorial concessions'.

LifeWay survey (2,002 Americans with evangelical beliefs, 20-28 Sep 2017; sponsored by Chosen People Ministries and Joel C. Rosenberg): 80% say Israel's 1948 rebirth fulfilled prophecy; 63% support Israel because 'God gave the land of Israel to the Jewish people'; 23% favour a Palestinian state treaty, 31% oppose, 46% unsure; support 58% (18-34) vs 77% (65+).

US Ambassador Mike Huckabee, Tucker Carlson interview aired 20 Feb 2026: on the Genesis promise (Nile to Euphrates), 'It would be fine if they took it all'; added Israel is not seeking to expand; 'Not sure we'd go that far'; Saudi: 'extremist rhetoric' and 'unacceptable'; Egypt: 'blatant violation' of international law; Arab League: 'extremist and lacking any sound basis'; Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, OIC condemned; no immediate US or Israeli comment.

Huckabee later called it 'somewhat of a hyperbolic statement', said 'They're not asking to take it over', said Carlson's posted version 'edited out my full response', said 'Area C is Israel'; State Department did not publicly address the remarks.

claims.text: Kach platform: 'Every Arab inside Israel is to be offered the right of residence as a non-citizen'; those who leave 'will receive compensation for their property'.
A.I. Kook was careful to express that the Kotel and the Temple Mount were holy sites that belong to the Jewish people, while opposing Jewish ascent under impurity laws.
Ynet: Zvi Yehuda Kook was the last speaker at the 1967 Independence Day event; student Yitzhak Shilat wrote he spoke 'with a rage and fury that I had never heard before'.

Zvi Yehuda Kook, 1974 lecture at Mercaz HaRav in Dayan's presence: yielding the Golan and West Bank would mean war 'over our bodies and limbs'; he opposed Begin's negotiations with Egypt because Sinai 'formed part of Biblical Israel'.
NPR: Smotrich calls the West Bank 'Judea and Samaria' and says it 'belongs to us'.
Oz VeShalom-Netivot Shalom (c. 1975) held that some religious Zionists made the state an end in itself, outranking 'justice, peace, and life itself'.

ABC: Huckabee described as an evangelical Christian and strong supporter of Israel and the West Bank settlement movement; Egypt's foreign ministry: 'blatant violation' of international law, 'Israel has no sovereignty over the occupied Palestinian territory or other Arab lands'.
Al Jazeera: Huckabee's 'Area C is Israel' appears to contradict the official US position opposing annexation; the State Department did not publicly address the remarks.

CUFI criticised by the Middle East Council of Churches and theologians in the Anglican and Catholic churches over its Christian Zionist and end-times theology; Hagee apologised for saying Hitler was fulfilling God's will.
Ben-Gvir, 23 July 2026: 'Look at what's happening here — Jews praying, feeling like they're the owners of the place.' 'This has never happened before.'
